reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses phase stability and irradiation resistance in other refractory HEAs (CrFeTiTaW, VFeTiTaW, MoNbTaW, etc.) but provides no data on oxide dispersion strengthening, Y2O3 stability in TiVNbTa, or the effects of Y2O3 on mechanical properties or thermal conductivity. The key premises about dispersion, thermal stability, strengthening, and property trade-offs are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nanoscale Y2O3 particles can be uniformly dispersed in TiVNbTa via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering without disrupting the single-phase BCC structure.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will remain thermally stable and not coarsen or form deleterious phases at ~1273 K.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles will impede dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding, increasing high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance.
A low volume fraction (<2 wt.%) of Y2O3 will not significantly degrade ductility or thermal conductivity.
